items.q: In the 'Types of RBC' note, the photographs labelled B and C belong to which category?
items.exp: Panel A is placed under urological (crenated and isomorphic cells), while panels B and C sit under Nephrological, carrying the dysmorphic cells and the acanthocytes. (Book p743)

items.q: Every dipstick row on this page has a clinical condition written against it EXCEPT:
items.exp: Leukocytes and nitrites share the UTI cell, urobilinogen is matched to extravascular hemolysis and glucose to proximal RTA and SGLT2 inhibitors; the protein, pH, blood, S.G, ketone and conjugated-bilirubin rows are left with a dash. (Book p743)

items.q: The leukocyte and nitrite rows of the dipstick table are printed as two tests sharing one clinical condition, urinary tract infection.
opts: True — the bracketed line 'high specificity, poor sensitivity' applies to that shared cell
False — nitrites alone carry the UTI entry
False — leukocytes are linked to extravascular hemolysis
True — and the same cell also lists proximal RTA
items.exp: The table merges Leukocytes and Nitrites against 'urinary tract infections (UTI) (High specificity, poor sensitivity)'. (Book p743)

items.q: All of the following are listed under 'Factors affecting leukocyte urine dipstick test' EXCEPT:
items.exp: The left-hand column reads concentrated urine, high relative density, proteinuria and glucosuria; the right-hand column lists cephalothin, tetracycline, cephalexin and tobramycin. (Book p743)

items.q: Match each dipstick row with the note printed in its condition cell — 1) Leukocytes and nitrites 2) Urobilinogen 3) Glucose … A) Proximal RTA and SGLT2 inhibitors B) Extravascular hemolysis C) High specificity, poor sensitivity
items.exp: The merged leukocyte/nitrite cell carries the 'high specificity, poor sensitivity' parenthetical; urobilinogen is paired with extravascular hemolysis; glucose with proximal RTA (euglycemic glycosuria) and SGLT2 inhibitors (euglycemic ketosis). (Book p743)
